chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil said:

Al-Tayyar said to Zurarah: 'What do you say about musahamah (drawing lots to decide a claim)? Is it not valid?' Zurarah said: 'Yes, it is valid.' Al-Tayyar said: 'Is it not that they have narrated that the lot of the truthful one (al-muḥiqq) comes out?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Come then, so I and you will claim something, then we will draw lots over it and see; is it like that?' Zurarah said to him: 'The hadith came specifically stating:
Among no people who entrust their affair to God and then draw lots, except that the lot of the truthful one comes out.

But regarding experience (al-tajārib), it was not placed upon experience.' Al-Tayyar said: 'Do you see if both are claimants and they claim what is not theirs, from where does the lot of one of them come out?' Zurarah said: 'If that is the case, a determining lot (sahm al-mubīḥ) is placed with it. If they both claim what is not theirs, the lot of the determining one comes out.'

key_terms.اَلْمُحِقّ: The truthful one (one whose claim is true)
key_terms.اَلْمُسَاهَمَة: Drawing lots to decide a claim or dispute
key_terms.سَهْمٌ مُبِيح: A determining lot (used to select one party when both claims are potentially false or equal)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence validate drawing lots (qur'a) to resolve legal disputes between two claimants?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Zurarah distinguishes between the general principle of *qur'a* (drawing lots) and its specific application in legal disputes, clarifying that the 'lot of the truthful' hadith refers to a context where parties entrust their matter to God, rather than a mechanical test of factual accuracy. He explains that when two parties make competing claims, the *sahm al-mubīḥ* (determining lot) serves as a divine mechanism to resolve the impasse, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that judicial *qur'a* is a valid, God-sanctioned method for establishing legal rights when evidence is balanced or indistinguishable.
